summary:
## Migrating a Large WordPress Site for Free

This document outlines the key steps to migrate a WordPress site of any size, including very large ones (e.g., 12GB+), for free using the **All-in-One WP Migration** plugin and a special workaround.

### ## Step 1: Export Your Website

1.  Install and activate the **All-in-One WP Migration** plugin on the source website.
2.  Navigate to `All-in-One WP Migration` > `Export`.
3.  Choose `Export to` > `File`.
4.  Wait for the process to complete and download the `.wpress` backup file.

### ## Step 2: Prepare the Destination Site

On the new, destination WordPress installation, perform a clean-up to avoid conflicts:

*   **Posts:** Delete all default posts.
*   **Pages:** Delete all default pages.
*   **Media:** Delete all items from the Media Library.
*   **Themes:** Delete all inactive themes.

### ## The Workaround: Bypassing the 300MB Upload Limit

The standard free version of the plugin limits imports to 300MB. To bypass this, you can use a modified version of the plugin, which is permissible under the **GPL version 3 license**.

> [!NOTE]
> The General Public License (GPL) allows users to modify and redistribute the source code of the plugin.

### ## Step 3: Install the Modified Plugin

1.  On the destination site, **deactivate and delete** the standard All-in-One WP Migration plugin if you installed it.
2.  Download the modified plugin from: `ferdykorp.com/migrate` (redirects to a Google Drive link from WP Press Doctor).
3.  Go to `Plugins` > `Add New` > `Upload Plugin` and upload the downloaded ZIP file.
4.  Activate the plugin. You now have an upload limit of up to **100GB**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Do not update this modified plugin, as updating will restore the 300MB import limit. After successfully migrating your site, it's a good practice to deactivate and delete the plugin.

### ## Step 4: Import and Finalize

1.  Go to `All-in-One WP Migration` > `Import`.
2.  Drag and drop your `.wpress` file to start the upload and import process.
3.  Click **Proceed** when prompted. This will overwrite the database, plugins, themes, and media.
4.  After the import is complete, you must log in with the **username and password from your original site**.
5.  Go to `Settings` > `Permalinks`, select **Post name**, and click **Save Changes twice** to rebuild your site's URL structure and prevent 404 errors.

### ## Alternative Use Cases

This method is also highly effective for:

*   **Creating full website backups:** Regularly export your site to a file for easy restoration.
*   **Migrating from local to live:** Develop your site on a local computer (e.g., using LocalWP) and use this process to push it to a live domain.
